plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stems carry huge golden-rimmed faces with dark, seed-packed centers. Entire fields turn together toward the sun, so the landscape looks like a sea of yellow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (roughly July through September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Northern Great Plains of the United States, and across Europe's sunflower-growing regions such as France, Hungary and Ukraine
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun from east to west during the day and swing back toward the east overnight. Mature blooms stop moving and generally face east.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: Tiny bell-shaped flowers blanket open moorland in waves of pink and purple. In late summer, hillsides across the uplands look as if they have been brushed with violet.
plants.location: Scottish Highlands, northern England moors and heathlands across northern Europe
plants.funFact: Heather is a vital late-summer nectar source, and bees feeding on it produce a dark, jelly-like honey with a strong, distinctive flavor.

plants.name: Hylotelephium spectabile
plants.description: Flat, dome-shaped clusters of star-like flowers sit above thick, blue-green leaves. They open pale pink and deepen toward rosy red as autumn approaches, and butterflies and bees crowd them.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn (August through October)
plants.location: Native to China and Korea, and widely grown in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Its fleshy leaves store water, so it thrives in dry spells. The dried flower heads stay attractive through winter.
